speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
current_text: The Appeals Court

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
current_text: The Appeals Court's Undersecretary Vellum, Mortimer's deputy, defends the transfer of authority to the last paragraph. He has never once been thanked. (Elite)

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
current_text: Undersecretary Vellum squares his papers and does not look up. "Noted. You wish to challenge the transfer of authority.

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
current_text: The authorization remains valid. It was submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized and filed. You may appeal in triplicate."

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
current_text: "Mr. Grimsby has asked me to hold the Court until his schedule opens. I will hold it very, very well. Noted."

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
current_text: Vellum squares his papers with great care. "Noted," he says, very quietly. "The authorization remains valid."

speaker: Undersecretary Vellum
current_text: For the first time, it sounds like a question.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: The Office of Final Approval

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: A vast office with a single desk, a single stamp, and one very patient authority.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No, looks up from an infinite pile of paperwork. His face is as smooth as a blank form. His stamp is the size of a tombstone.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: "You do not have an appointment. That is irregular. However, the authorization is valid, and under it every visitor is entitled to a hearing.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: The answer is no. The question is irrelevant. Please state your case anyway.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: You have, according to the clock, four hundred years."

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: The stamp falls from Mortimer's hand, and the paperwork goes still.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: At the very bottom of the pile, under every form, every stamp and every signature, is a small note in a trembling hand: FILED ON A TUESDAY.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: "...Oh," says Mortimer. "Oh, no. Tuesday is not a business day in this building.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: The authorization was valid. It was always valid. But the office is vacant, and policy is policy."

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Audit

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The auditor lays three cards on the Scale of Approved Expenditures. A reasonable total will be stamped. An unreasonable one will be fined.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Take a Number

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: You hold ticket 4,000,213. The display says NOW SERVING: 3. The queue snakes through the lobby, up the stairs and out of a window.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: A clerk offers you a form, a coffee and a pitying look.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Wait your turn (it will be a while)

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Pay the Expedite Fee (30 gold)

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Cut in line

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: You wait. And wait. A clerk takes pity, and the polite ghost ahead of you shares a biscuit and apologises that it is stale.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: You are called in, eventually, rested and a little richer. Waiting, in the Hall, is a kind of work.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: The Expedite Fee is an official fee, with an official receipt. A tiny clerk stamps your ticket and a door opens. You feel oddly refreshed.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: You cut in line. Forty thousand undead clerks turn and glare. You are processed immediately, and a little roughly.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Form 13-B

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: To pass the counter you need Form 13-B. The clerk says Form 13-B requires a Form 13-A, which she will gladly give you, once you have submitted Form 13-B.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Ask for Form 13-A

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Pay the clerk 25 gold to look the other way

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: "Form 13-A," she says. "Certainly. It requires a Form 12-F, which requires a strong cup of tea."

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: She does not look the other way. She looks at the gold. The gold is accepted.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: She stamps something you cannot read, and the way ahead opens.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Form 12-F

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Form 12-F is available at the Counter of Form 12-F. The Counter of Form 12-F is closed until Form 13-B has been filed.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Ask for Form 11-D

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Argue

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: "Form 11-D," she says. "A simple form. It requires only your signature, in blood.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Please do not worry. Blood is optional. The signature is not."

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: You argue. A tiny stamp appears from nowhere and hits you. It hurts a little.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: The clerk says: "That was a warning. The authorization is valid."

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Form 11-D

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Form 11-D is the last form in the chain. It is one line long: "I, the undersigned, request Form 13-B." You sign.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: A stamp thunders. Forms 13-B, 13-A and 12-F all appear at once, in perfect order.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Submit all the forms and claim the reward

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Rest in the clerk's break room instead

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Every form passes. A bureaucrat's tear of joy lands on the ink. You receive a stamped Form 13-B, a small refund and a commendation you cannot read.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: The clerk's break room is the most efficient room in the Hall. You are given a cup of tea, a biscuit and a lovely, quiet chair. You feel ready for the next department.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: The Notary's Counter

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: A very old notary sits behind a very high counter, a seal in one hand and a very large quill in the other. "Everything in the Hall," he says, "must be notarized.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Even you. Especially you."

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Get your credentials notarized (50 gold)

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Lie down in the notary's cot

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: Sell the notary a spare seal

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: The seal comes down with a THUMP. You are, officially, a person. Your units feel more legitimate, and hit a little harder for it.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: The cot is small, hard and incredibly comfortable. You sleep for a very official ten minutes, and wake refreshed, with the notary's seal printed on one cheek.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
current_text: He pays in cash, takes no receipt, and tells you he never saw you. You have never felt more notarized.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: The Records Labyrinth is a canyon of filing cabinets that goes down further than it goes up. At its heart, under glass, lies the original transfer: the Necrocrat Path, signed over to {villain}.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: It is flawless. Submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized, filed.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: Agnes reads over your shoulder and stops at one clause. Under HEIR OF THE FORMER SOVEREIGN it says: "Deceased (presumed). Remains: not on file."

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: "Irregular," says Agnes, very quietly, and looks at it for a long time. "A presumed death with no remains on file is an incomplete form.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: Somebody should look into that. ...Not me, dear. I'm only a ghost with a pencil."
new_text: Someone should look into it, dear. This form does not tell us what happened to the boy."
writer_note: Keeps missing-remains clue; removes joke beside presumed royal death.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
current_text: The CE-No has been removed from office. By policy, the vacancy passes to the senior-most applicant on file. One moment. I will look it up.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
current_text: ...It is a ghost. It is, for the record, you, Ms. Overdue.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: Me? Oh, for pity's sake. I filed more appeals than anyone alive or dead, and this is how they reward it?

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: I only ever wanted to leave.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
current_text: The procedure is clear. The office passes to you, and I am afraid you cannot appeal it. I would have to deny it.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: ...Then I will stay, Mortimer. Not for you. I will stay until nobody waits as long as I did.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: Even the dead deserve humanity. Our job is to help the lost souls. We have an obligation to help.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: Following orders be damned. We treat everyone with respect.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
current_text: ...That is not in the handbook.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
current_text: Then we write a new one. Take a number, Mortimer. You are right behind Gerald.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: Prudence Pallor, Deputy Head of the Department. Yes, I stamped DENIED on everything. I was tired, the paperwork was valid, and I am sorry.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: {villain} did not corrupt us, you know. He used our own rules. Now I stamp APPROVED on things that deserve it.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: The stamp is lighter than I remembered. Do you have anything I can approve?

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: Mortimer Grimsby. Formerly CE-No. Currently number 4,000,214 in the Waiting Room of Eternity. Gerald was 4,000,212.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: Number 4,000,213 was, I am told, you. You did not wait. I find I resent that, and I am told resenting it is healthy.
new_text: You had 4,000,213. You did not wait. I keep thinking about that.
writer_note: Preserves queue callback while making Mortimer confront what waiting means.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: I was very good at making others wait. I find I am much worse at it myself.
new_text: I made others wait far longer. It is worse knowing that now.
writer_note: Sincere aftermath; no punchline over the consequences of his rule.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
current_text: The authorization was valid. I have begun to wonder whether that was ever the right question.
